correctness.rationale: On a fixed Euclidean regular hexagon and exact reciprocal lattice, the piecewise polygon integral yields an analytic cosine quotient. At nonaxial integer lattice nodes its numerator has zero gradient and Hessian 4π²[[n,m−n],[m−n,−m]], strictly indefinite. After transformation to physical Cartesian frequencies, the leading quadratic term is an exact scalar multiple of Re[(ξ_x+iξ_y)(h_x+i h_y)^2], with nonzero coefficient; hence order two, harmonicity, and two perpendicular analytic Morse branches. At integer axial nodes explicitly nonzero linear jets give regularity. At noninteger dual cosets ∇N is ±π√3(2s−t,2t−s), nonzero. Lattice covolume/index and O(R) excluded axes give the claimed one-third density. Direct quadrature and exact symbolic checks, including 288 finite dual nodes, agree; finite checks are not the proof.

value.rationale: The reciprocal lattice is the natural forced-zero set of a hexagonal tiling/sampling kernel. Its exact local nodal types were not determined by the standard orthogonality condition: a full index-three family of degenerate harmonic zeros has two orthogonal branches, with angle varying by a nontrivial half-angle law, whereas the other sites are simple. The one-third incidence is a sharp complete natural invariant useful when studying diffraction nodal sets and regular hexagonal cardinal sinc kernels. This is a structural all-index classification rather than a renamed trigonometric identity or arbitrary finite data slice.
